title: What do you do?
titleSegs: your work, your job (to a man)
summary: Say what you and your family do for a living, with job words for men and for women.
intro: To ask about someone's job, say مَا عَمَلُكَ؟ (what is your work?) to a man, or مَا عَمَلُكِ؟ to a woman. Answer with a job word and no verb: أَنَا طَالِب (I am a student). A woman's job word usually adds ة: طَبِيب → طَبِيبَة.
objectives: Name seven jobs and two workplaces
Ask a man or a woman what they do
Say what your family does, e.g. أَبِي مُهَنْدِس
Make a job word feminine with ة

realLife.title: A lesson about jobs
realLife.story: Week two begins. Mr Karim asks his students what their parents do. Daniel talks about his family in Chicago and Layla about her mother, a nurse in Beirut. Then everyone is surprised to hear what Mr Karim does in the evenings.

sentences.en: What do you do? (to a man)
I am a student, and she is a student.
sentences.literal: I (am) a student, and she (is) a student

mistakes.why: She is a woman, so the job word takes ة: ṭāliba.

sentences.en: My father is an engineer at a big company.
sentences.literal: my father (is) an engineer in a company big

sentences.en: His mother is a doctor at the hospital.
sentences.literal: his mother (is) a doctor in the hospital

mistakes.why: A mother is a woman, so the job word is ṭabība, with ة.
Layla is a woman, so 'your' is the ending -ki, not -ka.

sentences.en: Mr Karim is a teacher and a translator.
sentences.literal: the teacher Karim (is) a teacher and a translator

dialogue.title: What do your parents do?
dialogue.culture: A teacher is called يَا أُسْتَاذ (to a man) or يَا أُسْتَاذَة (to a woman), and the same word is a polite title, like 'Mr' or 'Ms': الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم. In Egypt many people, like Mr Karim, have a second job in the evening.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر يَا طُلَّاب! الْيَوْم دَرْسُنَا عَنِ الْعَمَل.
lines.en: Good morning, students! Today our lesson is about work.

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، مَا عَمَلُكَ؟ هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِب فَقَطْ؟
lines.en: Daniel, what do you do? Are you only a student?
segs: your work, your job (to a man)

lines.ar: نَعَم يَا أُسْتَاذ، أَنَا طَالِب فِي مَدْرَسَةِ اللُّغَة هُنَا فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Yes, sir. I am a student at the language school here in Cairo.

lines.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَمَا عَمَلُ أَبِيكَ وَأُمِّكَ فِي شِيكَاغُو؟
lines.en: Excellent. And what do your father and mother do in Chicago?

lines.ar: أَبِي مُوَظَّف فِي شَرِكَة كَبِيرَة، وَأُمِّي مُهَنْدِسَة.
lines.en: My father is an employee at a big company, and my mother is an engineer.

lines.ar: جَمِيل! وَأَنْتِ يَا لَيْلَى؟ مَا عَمَلُ أَبِيكِ وَأُمِّكِ؟
lines.en: Lovely! And you, Layla? What do your father and mother do?

lines.ar: أُمِّي مُمَرِّضَة فِي مُسْتَشْفَى كَبِير فِي بَيْرُوت، وَأَبِي مُدَرِّس.
lines.en: My mother is a nurse at a big hospital in Beirut, and my father is a teacher.

lines.ar: مُدَرِّس مِثْلِي! وَأَنْتَ يَا سَامِي؟ أَبُوكَ مُهَنْدِس، صَحِيح؟
lines.en: A teacher like me! And you, Sami? Your father is an engineer, right?

lines.ar: نَعَم، أَبِي مُهَنْدِس، وَأُمِّي طَبِيبَة فِي مُسْتَشْفَى قَرِيب مِنْ بَيْتِنَا.
lines.en: Yes, my father is an engineer, and my mother is a doctor at a hospital near our house.

lines.ar: يَا سَامِي، هَلْ عِنْدَ أُمِّكَ عَمَل كَثِير فِي الْمُسْتَشْفَى؟
lines.en: Sami, does your mother have a lot of work at the hospital?

lines.ar: نَعَم، عِنْدَهَا عَمَل كَثِير كُلَّ يَوْم، مِنَ الصَّبَاح إِلَى الْمَسَاء.
lines.en: Yes, she has a lot of work every day, from morning to evening.

lines.ar: وَأَنْتَ يَا أُسْتَاذ كَرِيم؟ هَلْ أَنْتَ مُدَرِّس هُنَا فَقَطْ؟
lines.en: And you, Mr Karim? Are you only a teacher here?

lines.ar: لَا، أَنَا مُدَرِّس فِي الصَّبَاح، وَمُتَرْجِم فِي شَرِكَة فِي الْمَسَاء.
lines.en: No, I am a teacher in the morning, and a translator at a company in the evening.

lines.ar: مُتَرْجِم! هٰذَا عَمَل جَمِيل. أَنَا أَيْضًا أُرِيدُ هٰذَا الْعَمَل.
lines.en: A translator! That is a lovely job. I would like that job too.

lines.ar: إِذَنْ، اُدْرُسْ كَثِيرًا يَا دَانْيَال! وَالْآن، اِفْتَحُوا الْكُتُب مِنْ فَضْلِكُمْ.
lines.en: Then study hard, Daniel! And now, open your books, please.

reading.title: Jobs in our class
reading.ar: فِي صَفِّنَا طُلَّاب مِنْ أَمْرِيكَا وَلُبْنَان وَمِصْر. أَبُو سَامِي مُهَنْدِس، وَأُمُّهُ طَبِيبَة. أُمُّ لَيْلَى مُمَرِّضَة فِي بَيْرُوت. وَالْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم مُدَرِّس وَمُتَرْجِم.
reading.en: In our class there are students from America, Lebanon and Egypt. Sami's father is an engineer, and his mother is a doctor. Layla's mother is a nurse in Beirut. And Mr Karim is a teacher and a translator.

quiz.prompt: How do you say 'a female teacher'?
How do you ask a woman what she does?
In the dialogue, what does Mr Karim do in the evening?
Which word has a long ī?

completion: Well done! You can ask مَا عَمَلُكَ؟, talk about your family's jobs and make a job word feminine with ة.
